cells.tense: You're standing here with the pen, and the direction you're picking is getting your full weight.
cells.act: cut to the logic and act on it
cells.ask: Take the choice you keep circling and cut straight to its logic in one pass — what actually follows if you do it — then decide, without reopening it.
cells.core:
You know how to point yourself at something and mean it. That's running clean at the moment: the choice you're weighing gets your whole weight, not a trial run, and the enthusiasm lands on a real direction instead of spraying. You can see the next move plainly and take it without needing the whole map — confidence that came from having actually developed something, not borrowed certainty.

The part worth feeding now is the thinking underneath. Your gut already picked; let your mind catch up and sharpen it. Strip the noise off each option, follow what genuinely comes next, and take the cleaner line. You'll move faster, and anyone watching will trust the aim more when they can see it was reasoned, not just felt.
cells.sheetLine: The direction is real and your mind is keeping up with it.
cells.verb: lighting the fire before you know where it will go
cells.place: at the point where the choice gets made and the direction gets set

lint.detail: no visible act in the ask — could a camera see it?

cells.tense: You'll be pushing toward a future that hasn't arrived yet, and the pushing is getting past what's actually here.
cells.act: perceive it with fresh eyes before judging
cells.ask: Go back and look again at something you already decided against, this week, with no verdict attached — just see what is actually sitting there.
cells.core:
The fire is real, and it's running past the ground it's meant to light. You're aiming at outcomes that haven't shown up, forcing the next move before the current one has proven what it's made of. From inside it feels like momentum. From outside it can read as deciding before the information has landed — the direction set before anyone, you included, has had a look at the terrain.

What's scarce isn't drive. It's the pause that lets something register before the ruling. There's a kind of knowing that arrives when you stop arguing with the not-knowing and simply watch. Take something you dismissed and give it the eyes of someone seeing it the first time. The direction you pick after that will hold, because you actually saw what you were choosing.
cells.sheetLine: You're deciding before the thing has had a chance to show you what it is.
cells.verb: lighting the fire before you know where it will go
cells.place: at the point where the choice gets made and the direction gets set

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that's already behind you, still deciding whether to go through.
cells.act: tend the small thing and learn from it
cells.ask: Tend something living that you can put your hands on — a plant, a habit, a project's first piece — and let what it actually needs point you onward.
cells.core:
The choice-making has gone quiet. You can point at where you meant to go, but the weight behind it has drained out, and the fire that used to pull people along is banked. It isn't that you don't care. It's that the direction you set is sitting behind you now, and you haven't located the current to move it forward.

The way back doesn't run through pushing harder or deciding bigger. It runs through something small enough to hold, something with material needs you can meet. Pick a real thing and tend it with your hands. Watch what it does, not what you want it to do. That kind of attention refills what you're running on, and the direction you choose next will have somewhere to stand.
cells.sheetLine: The door is behind you and the next one opens through something you can tend.
cells.verb: lighting the fire before you know where it will go
cells.place: at the point where the choice gets made and the direction gets set

cells.tense: Right now you're choosing the direction, and the one choosing isn't showing up as the source.
cells.act: lay the one step you can see, solidly
cells.ask: Lay down the next single step you can actually see — not the whole path, just such a step — and build it solidly enough that it holds when you step back.
cells.core:
You're directing things. The energy goes somewhere chosen, and results show up as if they simply happened — schedules that work, decisions that stick, a direction that keeps holding. Ask who's steering and the answer sounds like circumstance, or just how things are. But the steering is yours, and you're not standing beside it.

What's called for isn't more vision. It's recognising that you're already building, and being willing to lay down one solid step you can actually see. Make the thing that lets the next thing happen, and make it to last. When it holds under weight, the fact that you made it becomes visible — to you first. The confidence that follows comes from having built, not from deciding to feel confident.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering, and the one steering isn't signing the work.
cells.verb: lighting the fire before you know where it will go
cells.place: at the point where the choice gets made and the direction gets set
